purpose: Representative source-observed semantic limitations, joined to the exhaustive explicit-unknown declared-export inventory; neither is full semantic review or runtime parity.

semantic_contract_classes.full_semantics: Behavior is intended to match the relevant POSIX, ISO C, GNU, or glibc contract for the supported scope and has fixture/proof/perf evidence elsewhere.
semantic_contract_classes.compat_noop: A symbol intentionally accepts the call and returns success or no observable action for compatibility, but does not implement the full upstream behavior.
semantic_contract_classes.deterministic_fallback: A symbol returns a deterministic fallback/error/fail-stop contract rather than the complete upstream behavior.
semantic_contract_classes.limited_bootstrap: A subsystem path implements a useful bootstrap subset while broader upstream semantics remain deferred.
semantic_contract_classes.unsupported_platform_contract: A historical or non-Linux surface deliberately returns ENOSYS or an equivalent unavailable status.
semantic_contract_classes.proof_gap: The status taxonomy may be correct, but there is insufficient fixture/proof/performance evidence for release-level parity claims.

coverage_policy.why_not_exhaustive: Declared exports are exhaustively accounted for by export_surface, but behavior/backend/configuration review is incomplete and remains unknown.
coverage_policy.release_blocker: Support labels and any Stub count, including Stub=0, are not semantic parity. Complete inventory does not complete semantic review or permit full replacement claims.

standalone_claim_guard.purpose: NSS bootstrap/fallback semantics are explicit L2/L3 standalone claim blockers until a full native backend set, nsswitch ordering, module fallback, and cache-coherence evidence are implemented.
standalone_claim_guard.user_visible_claim: NSS backend breadth remains L0/L1-only; standalone claims are blocked until files/backend/module-order/cache-coherence evidence passes.

audited_entries.evidence: Many files-plugin iteration hooks return deterministic SUCCESS/NOTFOUND/ENOENT fallbacks; protocol/service entries also have native iteration paths. The wildcard family is mixed and does not establish full NSS backend/module semantics.

Keep full semantic status unknown until the named behavior/configuration is actually qualified under bd-reality-202609-lx578q.7.

audited_entries.evidence: __nss_configure_lookup publishes owned runtime policies for passwd, group, shadow, initgroups, hosts, services, publickey and netgroup across the existing native/module dispatchers. The first successful override freezes the shared file image; invalid replacements preserve the prior policy. Private service_user traversal remains unavailable. The default-feature release DSO at d9d13977 passed the 106-case provider-pinned GNU differential in strict and hardened modes, and the concurrent replacement regression executed. Publickey/netgroup positive-provider and alternate-feature qualification remain open.
audited_entries.required_followup: Run the owned-TLS feature matrix and extend positive runtime provider coverage to publickey/netgroup. Qualify remaining GNU database names, service-token syntax, private traversal and standalone module loading under bd-reality-202609-lx578q.7; this mixed family remains semantically incomplete.

audited_entries.evidence: argp_help/state_help use the native tree renderer, filters and caller streams; state_help/usage can exit according to flags. Existing source is broader than the historical literal/no-exit subset; full GNU behavior remains unqualified by this inventory.

Qualify the declared GNU contract and owner policy, then implement and execute bounded local-server success/error cases under bd-reality-202609-lx578q.7 without assuming reserved-port helpers implement the remote protocol.

audited_summary.blocked_claim: The current support taxonomy contains 18 explicit Stub rows. The representative semantic inventory also retains no-op, fallback, bootstrap, unsupported, and under-proven surfaces; it is not exhaustive and cannot establish full replacement parity.
